function: Uplink channel estimation of the direct and RIS-cascaded channels from pilot observations, formulated as reverse diffusion with DDIM sampling started at an SNR-matched step (pp. 1-3).
system: Uplink: BS and passive reflecting RIS with half-wavelength UPAs, single-antenna UE; array sizes not stated; mmWave 28 and 73 GHz; InH and UMi scenarios (pp. 2, 4).
method: Diffusion model: DDIM sampling with step matching and a lightweight CNN-attention noise predictor (BRCNet) trained on simulated channel samples with a noise-prediction loss (pp. 3-4).
data_channel: Clustered statistical channel following 3GPP TR 38.901 [14] and SimRIS [15]; InH and UMi at 28 and 73 GHz; 50,000 training and 10,000 test samples per scenario (pp. 2, 4).
test_conditions: Trained on the training set of each scenario and tested on 10,000 held-out samples of the same scenario; SNR swept from -10 to 10 dB without retraining (pp. 4-5).
baselines: Non-learned: LMMSE, DS-OMP [3]. Learned: CDRN [4], LCDM CNN1 and CNN2 [10], GDM [11]; own variants with CNN2, U-Net, and no step-matching (pp. 4-5).
metrics: NMSE in dB versus SNR for four scenarios; number of parameters and MACs of the networks (pp. 4-5).
complexity: Table I: parameters and MACs; BRCNet 2.41M parameters and 2.18G MACs, U-Net 25.81M and 7.97G (p. 5).
q1_support: p. 2: "Following [14] and [15], a clustered statistical channel model is adopted." Reference [14] is 3GPP, p. 5: "Technical Report TR 38.901"; p. 4: "generation code is developed based on the open-source MATLAB simulator SimRIS [15]."
q2_support: p. 4: "For each scenario, the training set consists of 50,000 channel samples", each scenario is tested on its own test set; p. 4: "can adapt to varying noise conditions without retraining." is an SNR sweep. No train-on-one-scenario, test-on-another result.
q3_support: p. 4: "the following baselines: (i) the LMMSE estimator; (ii) DSOMP [3]; (iii) CDRN [4]" plus LCDM [10] and GDM [11], earlier learned estimators; all compared on NMSE in Fig. 3 (p. 5).
q4_support: p. 5: "Table I compares the number of parameters and the number of multiply-accumulate operations (MACs) of different" networks; Table I lists BRCNet at 2.41M parameters and 2.18G MACs.
q5_support: p. 4: "generation code is developed based on the open-source MATLAB simulator SimRIS [15]." The paper's own code and data are not released: no link or DOI appears in the 5 pages, and the channels come from a simulator, not a public dataset.
notes: q1 is 1 because the paper states that its clustered statistical channel follows [14], which is 3GPP TR 38.901, and [15] SimRIS, and that its data code is built on SimRIS; the reviewer may confirm that this reading meets the built-on-3GPP rule. q2 is 0: each scenario has its own training set, and the SNR sweep without retraining does not count by the rule. q5 is 0: SimRIS is open-source, but the paper links no code or data of its own, and I read SimRIS as a simulator, not a public dataset; the reviewer may weigh this. The BS and RIS array sizes and the number of pilot slots are not given in the text. The PDF is the arXiv v4 preprint (arXiv:2506.07770, 7 Jan 2026) and prints no DOI; it is identified by its title and topic.
